architecture.mechanism: Non-metallic inclusions, particularly MnS-containing inclusions, act as primary crack initiation sites in rolling contact fatigue (RCF) under electrical loading conditions, accelerating white etching crack (WEC) formation.
architecture.intervention: Modify the bearing steel composition of the intermediate-speed planet bearings to reduce MnS inclusion content and optimize the distribution of non-metallic inclusions, while maintaining hardness and overall inclusion levels similar to or better than Steel 1 in the study.
architecture.expected_effect: Extended bearing service life beyond 20 years by mitigating crack initiation at inclusion sites, reducing WEC formation, and improving resistance to electrically assisted fatigue under high slip conditions.
architecture.falsification_test: Conduct accelerated life testing on prototype bearings with modified steel composition (low MnS inclusions) and compare RCF life under DC electrical loading (5 conditions) and lubricated with WEC-forming gearbox oil against baseline bearings. Measure crack initiation sites and WEC formation via metallographic analysis after 100M cycles.
